cards.text: Jesus just finished teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. He told them He is the bread of life, and whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood has eternal life (John 6:54, 59). Now it's His own disciples huddled up, talking it over.

cards.question: Many of His disciples hear it and say, "This is a ___ teaching. Who can accept it?"
The disciples are grumbling about this teaching. True or false: somebody has to go tell Jesus about it.

cards.text: Nobody has to tell Him. Jesus asks them, "Does this offend you?" and then asks what will happen if they see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before.

cards.question: Jesus says the flesh profits nothing. He says the ___ is what gives life.

cards.text: Jesus says the words He has spoken to them are spirit and they are life. Then, right in front of everybody, He says some of them do not believe.

cards.question: John stops the story to tell us something about Jesus. True or false: Jesus had known from the beginning which of His disciples did not believe.
Jesus reminds His disciples of something He told them before. No one can come to Him unless what?

answers.text: The Father has granted it to him
He keeps every law of Moses
He was born a son of Abraham

cards.question: From that time on, what do many of Jesus' disciples do?

answers.text: Turn back and stop walking with Him
Stay and ask Him to explain it
Go back to the synagogue to argue

cards.text: Many of His disciples turn back and no longer walk with Him. That's not a couple of folks slipping out early, friend. That's MANY.

cards.question: With so many disciples gone, Jesus turns to the ___ and asks, "Do you want to leave too?"

cards.text: Simon Peter, one of the Twelve, speaks up: "Lord, to whom would we go?" He answers a question with a question, and somehow it's the best answer in the room.

cards.question: Why does Peter say there's nowhere else for the Twelve to go?

answers.text: Jesus has the words of eternal life
Jesus fed thousands with five loaves
Jesus healed so many of the sick

cards.question: Peter goes on and tells Jesus what the Twelve believe and know about Him. What is it?

answers.text: He is the Holy One of God
He is a prophet like Moses
He is a teacher from Capernaum

cards.text: Jesus answers them: He chose them, the Twelve. And then He says something so heavy I'd have dropped every cookie box in my mustache.

cards.question: Jesus reminds the Twelve that He chose them. True or false: He also says one of them is a devil.
John tells us exactly which one of the Twelve Jesus was speaking about. Who is it?
Judas was one of the Twelve, but later he was going to ___ Jesus.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "This is a ___ teaching. Who can accept it?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus told them He is the bread of life, but it only cites John 6:54 and 6:59. 'I am the bread of life' comes from John 6:35 and 6:48, and neither verse is cited.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The opening card is plain narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice or humor. Cards 4 and 6 have the same problem (see the next finding).

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This story card only retells Jesus' two questions in flat summary. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice, even though Jesus knowing about the grumbling without being told is a moment that could hold a real laugh. Card 6 has the same problem.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 9 already asked about and revealed John 6:66, that many disciples turn back and no longer walk with Him. Card 10 restates the same verse and adds no new moment, so it is a recap card. The joke could move onto a card that carries the passage forward.

The setup says Jesus is about to say 'something so heavy I'd have dropped every cookie box in my mustache.' Card 16 then asks True or False whether He says one of them is a devil. The setup tells the baker a shocking statement is coming, which points to True and rules out False.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Cards 7 and 17 name the narrator as John ('John stops the story', 'John tells us'). The Gospel never names its author, and the cards give no reference for this.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin name John as the Gospel's narrator without a reference, or should these cards say something neutral like 'the Gospel stops the story'?
